title: RAW attraction mode constrains material priority without one universal ranking
summary: RAW_UNREVIEWED_NOT_SELECTED_NOT_EXECUTED. Galen distinguishes light-first vacancy filling from quality attraction that may favor heavier suitable matter. The final wine case retains physical mobility as a further factor, so the proposed content is a mode-scoped priority statement rather than a universal selection algorithm.

design.question: Can an explicitly written mode and scope control a priority or permission relation over candidate matter while keeping attraction as a shared operation kind?
design.source_locus: III14 water/sand tube example, III15 opening bellows/lodestone comparison (pp317–321), and the closing wine/artery paragraph (pp329–331).
design.source_content: Evacuation draws lighter matter before heavier matter. Attraction through qualitative suitability may act on the heavier candidate when it is more naturally related. Later, suitability and thinness jointly enter the comparison of absorption.
design.unknown_after_source: No target attraction term, mode marker, candidate comparison, ordering expression or modal operator is bound. It is unknown whether this content is expressed compositionally, through separately named operations, or at all.

proposed_content_schema.DECLARE_MODE: DECLARE_MODE(attraction_description, mechanism_mode, receiver, availability_context) retains the attraction kind and explicitly states the relevant mechanism and situation. A mode name is not a target morphology claim.
proposed_content_schema.VACANCY_PRIORITY: Within the described accessible candidate context, the source's vacancy-filling account orders lighter/thinner matter before heavier/thicker matter. Candidate availability and access are explicit; inaccessible light material cannot be invented.
proposed_content_schema.QUALITY_PERMISSION: Within a quality-attraction description, a heavier candidate may be selected when it is more appropriate to the receiver. This is not the universal statement that the heaviest, or even the most appropriate, always arrives first.
proposed_content_schema.MOBILITY_QUALIFICATION: A later assertion may qualify uptake by thinness, vessel width and attractive efficiency when these are actually written. The source's quality mechanism does not cancel the final paragraph's mobility conditions.
proposed_content_schema.composition: A shared attraction description plus an explicit mode permits different priority/modal assertions. Removing the mode cannot preserve both a universal lighter-first rule and the quality account unchanged.
proposed_content_schema.noncollapse: Lightness, suitability and mode are separate predicates. No one-dimensional good/bad score, numerical force law, fixed threshold or deterministic winner is supplied.

connected_cases.input: The source's tube in a water-and-sand vessel under evacuation.
connected_cases.consequence: With the stated accessible candidates, water precedes sand. This combines the event mode and the material ordering; it is not an arbitrary lexical substitution.

connected_cases.input: A quality-attraction description with a heavier but more naturally related candidate; lodestone/iron illustrates the distinct kind of action.
connected_cases.consequence: A heavier candidate is permitted by the account. This modal claim contradicts a universal lighter-first rule for every attraction, but does not assert every such candidate wins. The source examples are not a controlled same-receiver intervention.

connected_cases.input: The closing account compares suitability and thinness, and notes several contributing conditions.
connected_cases.consequence: A quality-attraction reading that makes uptake wholly independent of physical mobility loses source content. No hypothetical example is allowed to erase that limit.

rivals.name: Universal lighter-first attraction
rivals.contract: All attraction uses the same lightness priority, regardless of mechanism.
rivals.distinguishing_consequence: It cannot express the source's explicit permission for heavier but suitable matter without adding a second criterion or mode.

rivals.name: Suitability always dominates all other factors
rivals.contract: Quality attraction deterministically chooses the most suitable candidate and ignores thickness or route conditions.
rivals.distinguishing_consequence: It overstates the qualified heavier-matter statement and cannot retain the final wine comparison unchanged.

rivals.name: Separately named attractive operations
rivals.contract: Use distinct operation nouns and independent clauses rather than one shared attraction base plus a mode construction.
rivals.distinguishing_consequence: This can preserve all source facts; only a complete written shared construction could favor the proposed reuse. Source facts alone do not select an encoding.

costs.unbound: All target modes, candidates, receivers, comparison scopes, availability relations, priority/modal assertions and their written order.

design.known_overlap: IDEA000577 already addresses owner/compartment/supply-case distinctions, and IDEA000541 concerns same-channel reversal. Neither distinction is novelty here. This card isolates mode-scoped candidate priority; it inherits no577 dictionary or541 transport direction. design.minimum_next_step: First compare exact mode/priority/comparator predecessors. If a distinction remains, author one complete admitted unit that writes both the attraction description and its mode/priority scope, preserving the mobility qualification rather than hiding it in commentary.
design.decision_changing_result: A stable written mode construction changing the allowed priority statement would constrain a complete hypothetical account. If only separate arbitrary names fit, construction choice remains unresolved. A fixed descendant that universalizes heavier-first or deletes mobility is unsupported and must not be repaired after testing.
